label: POSSIBLE INTERPRETATION
text: Case B conditions (see the Case B finding) may arise because a Random Forest predicts from many columns at once, and unaffected columns such as lat, long and sqft_living15 carry much of the price signal, whereas each OLS coefficient depends on how the one affected column was filled. This was not tested here; it could be examined by checking how prediction changes when only one affected column is imputed at a time.

label: POSSIBLE INTERPRETATION
text: If predictive differences between imputers are small relative to repeat noise, one possible reason is a ceiling effect: the always-observed columns (lat, long) and correlated columns (sqft_living15 with sqft_living) may let the forest recover most of the signal whatever is imputed. This was not tested; dropping those columns in a side experiment would test it.

label: POSSIBLE INTERPRETATION
text: Significance flips were expected to be rare because n stays near 21,000, but for complete-case analysis they occur. A possible reason is that deleting rows lowers n and widens the intervals, so borderline coefficients change status; the number of rows kept is reported in the statistical findings. This was not tested.

label: POSSIBLE INTERPRETATION
text: Complete-case error is larger under MAR than MCAR at most levels. Member 1 suggested this may partly reflect an imperfect linear model (the dropped rows depend on long, which the linear model captures only partly). That guess is untested and is not a finding of this study.
